subject: Strange behaviour in session control or environment control?

messages.author: ac2d2e4dc0e3cb16
messages.subject: Strange behaviour in session control or environment control?
parts:
I use rapache for generation of questionnair reports.
Now as a test I had the following simple brew script:

<%
print(ls())
%>

I would expect that on each call a new session is started up, so that this always prints an empty list(character(0). I suppose the user is www-data, and this user does not have a ~/.RData file
If the script is called several times, however, sometimes (or often), a list of objects is displayed, probably from another session. You can try this at http://www.dpvragenlijst.nl/z/boe

Is this intended behaviour? I can not expect that. And is there a way to prevent this? This appears to be very dangerous.

Is this the same problem as in https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rapache/vAQot_kzEIM ?

Thanks

Frans

messages.author: ac2d2e4dc0e3cb16
messages.subject: Re: Strange behaviour in session control or environment control?
parts:
I hope that I am making a mistake, but if I am right, there is a serious problem. On itself it is no big problem that the process sees an existing environment. My programs depend on the GET parameters, however. I have the following test script:
<pre>
<%
print(str(GET))
print(ls())
%>
</pre>

if I run this with http://www.dpvragenlijst.nl/z/boe2?name=frans , let's say 10 times, this also gives incorrect results for GET sometimes. If this is indeed so, we cannot trust the results.
Thanks for your reactions.

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Re: Strange behaviour in session control or environment control?
parts:
I know this might seem strange when you first learn this, but its a property of rApache applications. The web server creates many child processes which all serve many clients.

If you want to maintain state per client then you'll need to build that layer yourself. A popular approach is to set a cookie in the client browser with a unique Id and store the client state keyed off the Id in a database.

rApache is a foundational layer that web application frameworks sit on top of. Although none exist right now, I'm hopeful someone may come along and write one.

Best,

Jeff

messages.author: ac2d2e4dc0e3cb16
messages.subject: Re: Strange behaviour in session control or environment control?
parts:
Hi masters of R
I found out what happened. I would not call it error, but it is really "unexpected behaviour".
The script is called with something like. "//www.dpvragenlijst.nl/z/boe?boem=ho"  Then GET$boem has the value "ho" But when the script is called without a parameter, I wanted a default value. For that reason I have the statement "if (is.null(GET)) {GET<-list();GET$boem<-"default value"}
This causes the problem: the environment may have a GET object from another session. And then GET does not have the expected value (the script is called without a parameter, but GET still has a value.

So probably the lesson is to never create a GET object, just read it.

What I still do not understand: what kind of object is GET? print(class(GET)) indicated GET is a list. But print(ls()) does not show it?
